item.title: Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews
item.description: Paris-based international press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday called on France's media regulator Arcom to suspend right-wing channel CNews for one month over its failure to uphold pluralism. The news channel owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré condemned the call for its suspension.

item.title: Will Spain's far right replace Europe's left-wing stalwart?
item.description: Some 39 million Spaniards will head to the ballot this Sunday to vote in early general elections. Latest polls put the conservative Popular Party ahead of incumbent PM Pedro Sanchez’s Socialists. The third-strongest political force, however, is the far-right Vox party. A strong showing at Sunday’s election could see them form Spain’s next government. FRANCE 24 explains.

item.title: ACROSS AFRICA: Tunisian Photographer's Family Focus
item.description: Stories from the continent with Georja Calvin-Smith. This week, health workers struggling to keep pace with DR Congo's Ebola outbreak say they feel abandoned and unsupported. Also, the World Cup was about more than winning... for some fans, at least. Tunisia's performance may not have been all that its supporters had hoped, but sports photographer Hosni Manoubi is far from negative about a family tradition of documenting his country's international sports showings. [Archive Episode, June 2026]

item.title: In California, exceptional tides and nearly 9m-high waves batter the coast
item.description: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.

item.title: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB
item.description: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). His nomination comes as the Europe's most powerful financial institution grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and a cost of living crisis.
